newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania aims to boost coffee production.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania aims to boost coffee production.

text.p: The Tanzanian government has announced a major programme to double annual coffee production to an estimated 100,000 tonnes by the year 2000, the state-owned Sunday News reported.
The Agriculture minister was quoted as saying the programme would involve replanting of aged coffee tress and the opening of new coffee farms.
The government would allocate 50 million shillings ($84,700) to establish plant nurseries and to educate farmers in the best production techniques, the minister said.
Industry representatives told Reuters that a large-scale replanting was needed to halt a decline in production, which had fallen by 20 percent in recent years.
The Tanzanian Coffee Board manager said production for the 1996/97 crop year, which started this month, was estimated at between 41,000 and 43,000 tonnes, against 53,000 tonnes in 1995/96.
Industry sources said the expansion programme would be centered in the Moshi area of northern Tanzania, where the valuable high-altitude Arabica coffee is grown.
They said the region has ample capacity to process a larger crop. ($=590 shilling)
